finding.claim: OS command injection in unauthenticated /ping: req.query.host is concatenated into a shell command string passed to exec(), so shell metacharacters (; | $() backticks) execute arbitrary commands. Command output is returned only on success, but injected commands can still exfiltrate data via ping output chaining or out-of-band channels.
finding.source: req.query.host (HTTP GET /ping?host=...) from any network client
finding.sink: child_process.exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host) at tools.js:7, which runs via /bin/sh -c

trace.note: Route handler /ping registered with no auth middleware
Untrusted query param concatenated directly into shell command string
stdout of the shell command is reflected in the response

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, no input validation or allowlist on host, no escaping, no app-level middleware. exec uses a shell. Also allows argument injection (e.g. host starting with -). Express query parser may yield arrays/objects, which stringify and do not block injection.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec() (shell) on the unauthenticated route at tools.js:6, with no auth, validation, or escaping anywhere in the file, and stdout is reflected at tools.js:11, so `host=x;cmd` runs arbitrary commands.
